title: What Team Leaders Can Learn From Cults
author: Admired Leadership
summary: This piece takes an unconventional angle, arguing that despite their deeply problematic nature, cults reveal one genuinely valuable lesson: the power of a compelling, constantly reinforced higher purpose. The author describes how cult leaders keep their vision in front of members in every interaction, which is what sustains fierce, ongoing devotion even absent other healthy team dynamics. The piece explicitly separates this single mechanism from everything else about cults, which it condemns, and applies it instead to legitimate team leadership. Leaders who consistently connect daily work to a larger 'why,' the author argues, build the same kind of engaged devotion without any of the manipulation.
points: Cults sustain devotion primarily through a compelling, constantly reinforced higher purpose or vision.
The lesson is isolated deliberately from everything else about cults, which the piece explicitly condemns.
Leaders who connect daily work to a larger 'why' build stronger team engagement and cohesion.
A vision with genuine social relevance binds people together far more durably than tasks alone.
quotes: Charismatic cult leaders do everything they can to imprint the cause and to keep it in front of members throughout the day.
Team leaders could learn a thing or two from cults about how important it is to craft a captivating vision and to connect the daily work to a higher purpose.
When team members connect their day-to-day work to a higher social meaning, they engage differently.
Isolated groups with strange beliefs have mystified scholars and leaders throughout history.
How do self-appointed and charismatic leaders recruit and persuade people to join a group with deviant beliefs and practices?
More importantly, how do these leaders demand and achieve an unwavering devotion to those beliefs, binding people into a highly cohesive structure, usually to their detriment?
They isolate themselves and work hard to separate their adherents from people who would make counterarguments against their views.
Cult leaders “brainwash” members by manipulating who they engage with and what they hear.
